recommendations.marketOutlook: War-driven regime with extreme fear (F&G 19) and negative gamma creating amplified moves in both directions. The S&P bounced 6% last week on ceasefire hopes, but breadth divergence (only 48.3% above 200 DMA) warns this is narrow, fragile leadership. March CPI on April 10 is the next major macro catalyst — oil pass-through could push inflation expectations higher and kill remaining rate cut hopes. The dominant trade remains long energy/gold/defense, short airlines/consumer, but the range-bound regime with elevated VIX means forcing trades carries high risk. Binary outcomes (ceasefire vs. escalation) make position sizing critical.

recommendations.catalyst: Range-bound regime with 39% confidence, extreme binary risk (ceasefire vs. escalation), negative gamma amplification, and CPI in 4 days
recommendations.reasoning: SIGNAL's highest-conviction candidate (DAL short into earnings) scores 74 composite — below the regime-mandated minimum of 78. The range-bound regime with -5 penalties on both longs and shorts, combined with extreme binary geopolitical risk (Iran ceasefire vs. escalation could move markets 5%+ in either direction), negative dealer gamma (amplified moves), and March CPI on April 10, creates an environment where the EXPECTED VALUE of forcing a trade is negative. Every candidate either: (a) has poor risk/reward at current levels (XOM near resistance, GDX 28% above 50-DMA, LMT at consensus PT), (b) faces binary event risk that makes stop placement unreliable (DAL earnings, ceasefire headlines), or (c) lacks sufficient timing urgency for a day trade (CCJ, AMD, LLY). Cash is a position. The disciplined move is to wait for either: a ceasefire resolution (then aggressively short energy/gold, long airlines), an escalation confirmation (then aggressively long energy/gold), or a CPI print that provides macro clarity.
recommendations.bearCase: Missing a 3-5% move in energy or gold if escalation accelerates before we can enter

recommendations.catalyst: Q1 earnings April 8 pre-market. Jet fuel costs +103% MoM devastate margins. Wide guidance ($0.50-$0.90) signals management uncertainty. Put/call skew confirms bearish positioning.
recommendations.reasoning: DAL reports Q1 earnings on April 8 pre-market with jet fuel at $195/bbl (up 103% in a month). Most airlines abandoned fuel hedging — DAL's refinery provides partial buffer but cannot offset a doubling of fuel costs. The EPS guide of $0.50-$0.90 is extremely wide, signaling management uncertainty. Options market confirms bearish sentiment (IV30 at 54.6, top 25% of year, put preference). The stock bounced from $55.20 to $66.70 — a 20% recovery that appears premature given the fuel cost reality. Regime underweight airlines. Short trades carry -5 penalty but the catalyst is binary and clear.
recommendations.bearCase: Delta's refinery hedge performs better than expected; forward guidance emphasizes pricing power and premium revenue streams; ceasefire hopes provide macro relief; short squeeze on heavily-shorted airline names.
